instruction: Adjust the system volume on my desktop down to 25 percent.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command:
pulseaudio --start
pactl list sinks | grep '^[[:space:]]Volume:' | head -n 1 | awk '{print $5}' | sed 's/%//g'

metadata.explanation: Task requires lowering the system volume to 25%. Evaluator uses existing exact_match metric with vm_command_line getter to check PulseAudio volume is '25\n'. No custom functions needed - reusing official evaluator components.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: vm_command_line executes PulseAudio command chain that properly extracts volume percentage (pactl list sinks | grep Volume | awk | sed removes %)
Metric comparison is appropriate: exact_match correctly compares volume string '25\n' with expected value
Data flow is sound: Command output (string) matches expected type, comparison will work at runtime
State accessibility is good: System volume is persistent and queryable via PulseAudio without needing postconfig
Expected value format relies on exact shell output: '25\n' assumes command returns '25' with trailing newline, which is standard but could vary if PulseAudio output format changes

Minor semantic gap: Instruction says 'lower' volume (implies directional change) but evaluator only checks final state is 25% (doesn't verify it was actually lowered from higher value). This is acceptable for most cases.

Edge case handling could be better: If PulseAudio outputs different format (e.g., '25.0%' or multiple sinks with different volumes), the awk field extraction might fail. Using head -n 1 assumes first sink is the target.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider making command more robust: Could add error handling for cases where PulseAudio is not running or volume format differs
Consider verifying directional change: If 'lower' is critical, could check initial volume > 25% before task execution (though this adds complexity)
Expected value is correct but fragile: '25\n' works for standard shell output but consider if whitespace variations could occur
